question: The National Food and Security Act of 2013 (NFSA2013) provides subsidised food grains to _______ of India's rural population.
solution:
The correct answer is __**75%.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The National Food and Security Act of 2013 (NFSA2013) provides subsidized food grains to 0.75 (75%) of India's rural population.**
 
• This Act aims to provide food security to the vulnerable sections of society by **ensuring access to adequate quantities of quality food at affordable prices.**
 
• The beneficiaries of the Act are identified as per the **Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011 data**.
 
• The Act provides 5 kg of food grains per person per month at a** highly subsidized price of Rs. 3 for rice, Rs. 2 for wheat, and Rs. 1 for coarse grains.**
 
• The NFSA 2013 also covers 50% of the urban population for subsidized food grains.
 
• The Act also provides for the setting up of a** grievance redressal mechanism at the district and state levels to ensure transparency and accountability in the implementation of the Act.**
 
• The Act has faced criticism for its exclusion criteria, which has led to **many eligible beneficiaries being left out of the system.**
 
• The Act has also faced challenges in terms of leakages and diversion of food grains meant for the beneficiaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The government notified the National Food Security Act, 2013 on 10th September 2013.
 
• It has the objective to provide food and nutritional security in the human life cycle approach, by ensuring access to an adequate quantity of quality food at affordable prices to people to live a life with dignity.
 
• The government of India enacted the National Food Security Act (NFSA) in July 2013 which gives legal entitlement to 67% of the population (75% in rural areas and 50% in urban areas) to receive highly subsidized foodgrains.
 
• The Act provides for coverage of up to 75% of the rural population and up to 50% of the urban population for receiving subsidized food grains under the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS), thus covering about two-thirds of the population.
 
• The National Food Security Act, 2013 (NFSA 2013) converts into legal entitlements for existing food security programs of the Government of India.
 
 
• It includes the Midday Meal Scheme, Integrated Child Development Services Scheme, and the Public Distribution System.
 
 
 
• The Act also has a special focus on nutritional support for women and children.
